title: Stop trying to get rich, get better: build product back to front to compound LTV and referrals
summary: Hormozi argues most small businesses are stuck in the "selling business", pouring leads into a leaky bucket. Instead, spend the early phase perfecting the product, so referrals, repeat purchase and brand cut CAC and raise LTV as you scale. He also covers finding activation points from retained customers and why the first phase is to learn, not earn.

principles.text: Getting rich is an output; getting better is the input. Focus on the input that creates wealth.
principles.quote: Getting rich is an outcome; getting better is an input.

principles.text: Lead shortage is usually a product problem: you can't afford leads because the product doesn't retain or generate referrals.
principles.quote: The problem is not that you don’t have enough leads; the problem is you can’t afford them because your product sucks.

principles.text: Win the LTV game: whoever makes customers most valuable can outspend on acquisition.
principles.quote: I rephrase that as, ‘He who can make his customers the most valuable wins,’

principles.text: Ad costs rise and efficiency falls at scale, so you need a compounding vehicle like referrals to hold LTV:CAC.
principles.quote: You need an equally strong compounding vehicle that works in your favor to maintain your LTV-to-CAC ratio.

principles.text: In the first phase, learn rather than earn: nail the model so customers stay and growth never stops.
principles.quote: The point in the first phase is to learn, not to earn.

principles.text: Find activation points by studying customers who don't cancel, then drive onboarding toward that experience.
principles.quote: Everything is about looking at the people at the end, looking at the thing that preceded them getting to that point, and then putting all of your focus on getting people to have that experience.
